teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: Unapproved audio-dependent test; original clip must be independently checked.

objective.q: Why does Ford mix a joke with memories of difficult years?
options: To show that his career was never important to him.
To make his account friendly while admitting that success took time.
To suggest every actor should work in carpentry.
To explain why he did not expect to attend the ceremony.
objective.explanation: Humour softens the reflection on a long and uncertain career.
objective.sourceEvidence: He jokes about the award and later describes years of struggle.

objective.q: What did Ford gain when he met the people putting on plays?
options: A chance to become a professional director at once.
A guaranteed job after college.
A new family business in carpentry.
A place where he felt he belonged.
objective.explanation: The anecdote stresses community and direction, not instant success.
objective.sourceEvidence: He found his people in a theatre group at college.

objective.q: What is Ford's point when he thanks people behind his films?
options: A successful film needs contributions from many people.
Only actors should be recognised by awards.
Most film jobs are less important than the leading role.
A good performance can replace the work of a film crew.
objective.explanation: His gratitude frames filmmaking as collaborative work.
objective.sourceEvidence: He thanks writers, directors, cast and crew.

objective.q: What does his story about the long wait before success suggest?
options: The beginning of a career is always the most enjoyable part.
Good acting can be learned without any practical work.
Progress may require patience and more than one kind of work.
Famous people usually know exactly where they will end up.
objective.explanation: Ford spent years struggling and doing carpentry between acting jobs.
objective.sourceEvidence: He describes about fifteen years before his breakthrough.

objective.q: Why does Ford talk about the importance of stories?
options: They help audiences connect with experiences and feelings.
They are more valuable than everyone who creates them.
They are mainly useful when a story is about a famous person.
They always teach viewers one simple lesson.
objective.explanation: Ford describes storytelling as a source of shared emotion.

objective.q: What responsibility does Ford connect with being successful?
options: Being more competitive with younger actors.
Keeping the same roles throughout a career.
Explaining every career decision in public.
Giving other people opportunities to succeed.
objective.explanation: He encourages established artists to support newcomers.
objective.sourceEvidence: Success brings freedom and a responsibility to others.

written.q: How does the story from college help explain Ford's choice of career?
written.modelAnswer: Finding a theatre group made Ford feel he belonged and gave acting a clearer purpose.
written.teacherCriterion: One supported link between a theatre community and his sense of career direction.
written.sourceEvidence: Ford finds people staging plays at college.

written.q: Give one example of the way Ford shares credit for his success.
written.modelAnswer: He thanks particular collaborators or describes the importance of cast, writers, directors and crew.
written.teacherCriterion: One concrete supported example of thanking or recognising other people.
written.sourceEvidence: Ford gives credit to multiple colleagues and supporters.
